"""csvlite: a tiny, self-contained CSV string parser.

Parses RFC-4180-style CSV text, honouring double-quoted fields so that
embedded commas, doubled quotes (``""``) and quoted newlines stay inside
a single field. Lines may be terminated by ``\n``, ``\r\n`` or ``\r``.
"""

__all__ = ["parse_csv"]


def parse_csv(text):
    """Parse *text* (a CSV document) into a list of rows.

    Each row is a list of strings. A field wrapped in double quotes may
    contain commas, carriage returns and newlines; a doubled double
    quote (``""``) inside such a field stands for one literal quote.

    >>> parse_csv('a,b\\\\n1,"x, y"\\\\n2,"he said ""hi""\\\\nbye"')
    [['a', 'b'], ['1', 'x, y'], ['2', 'he said "hi"\\\\nbye']]
    """
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        raise TypeError(
            "parse_csv() expects a str, got %s" % type(text).__name__
        )

    rows = []
    row = []
    field = []
    state = "start"  # start-of-field | unquoted | quoted | after closing quote
    row_started = False
    i = 0
    n = len(text)

    while i < n:
        ch = text[i]

        if state == "quoted":
            # Inside a quoted field every character is literal, including
            # commas, carriage returns and newlines.  A quote either
            # closes the field or, when doubled, is one literal quote.
            if ch == '"':
                state = "after_quote"
            else:
                field.append(ch)
            row_started = True
            i += 1
            continue

        if ch == '"':
            if state == "start":
                state = "quoted"  # opening quote is not part of the field
            elif state == "after_quote":
                field.append('"')  # doubled quote -> one literal quote
                state = "quoted"
            else:
                # Stray quote inside (or after) an unquoted field stays
                # literal and does not open a quoted field.
                field.append(ch)
                state = "unquoted"
            row_started = True
        elif ch == ",":
            row.append("".join(field))
            field = []
            state = "start"
            row_started = True
        elif ch == "\n" or ch == "\r":
            # Row separator (only reached outside a quoted field).
            if row_started:
                row.append("".join(field))
                rows.append(row)
            else:
                rows.append([])  # blank line -> empty row
            row = []
            field = []
            state = "start"
            row_started = False
            if ch == "\r" and i + 1 < n and text[i + 1] == "\n":
                i += 1  # consume the "\n" of a "\r\n" pair
        else:
            field.append(ch)
            state = "unquoted"
            row_started = True
        i += 1

    # Flush the final row; a trailing line terminator adds no extra row.
    if row_started:
        row.append("".join(field))
        rows.append(row)

    return rows
